chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) and asked him about a man who frees a young slave or an old man, or someone who is incapacitated and has no means of support. He said: 'Whoever frees a slave who has no means of support, then it is upon him to provide for him until he becomes self-sufficient. And this is what Ali (peace be upon him) used to do when he freed young slaves and those who had no means of support.'
ai.seo_question: What is the obligation of a master who frees a slave who cannot support themselves?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the financial liability (*nafaqah*) of the emancipator, establishing that freeing a dependent slave creates an ongoing obligation to support them until self-sufficiency is achieved. It highlights the *Sunnah* of Imam Ali (AS), demonstrating that this legal principle was not merely a theoretical ruling but a consistent practice of the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby reinforcing its authority in Shia jurisprudence.
